name: What should I know about waterproofing a shower in a bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: What should I know about waterproofing a shower in a bathroom remodel so it does not leak later?
mainEntity.text: What should I know about waterproofing a shower in a bathroom remodel so it does not leak later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waterproofing is one of the most important parts of a bathroom remodel because tile alone does not stop water. A properly built shower needs a complete waterproofing system behind or under the finish surface, with special attention to seams, corners, benches, niches, valves, and drain connections. The goal is to keep water out of the wall cavity and subfloor so the structure does not rot over time. Homeowners should ask what waterproofing system will be used, how it is tested, and whether the contractor includes flood testing when appropriate. This matters even more in luxury remodels, because expensive tile and fixtures can still fail if the waterproofing is weak. If a contractor treats waterproofing as a minor step, that is a warning sign. A beautiful shower that leaks is never a good value. Ask for a clear explanation of the process before materials are approved.
acceptedAnswer.description: Shower waterproofing should protect every vulnerable surface, including the floor, walls, seams, corners, niches, and penetrations. The shower must be built so water reaches the drain instead of the structure behind the tile. Good waterproofing is one of the most important parts of a lasting remodel.
